To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conformal field theories in four dimensions with a unique stress-energy tensor and at least two conserved currents of spin 2 and s>2, are completely fixed by the requirement that the currents are conserved, and by the requirement that their two-point functions are fixed to be equal to the two-point functions of the currents of the free field theories.

(i) the existence of a unique stress tensor in four dimensions implies the existence of infinitely many higher spin conserved currents, (ii) the existence of infinitely higher-spin conserved charges implies that the theory must be a free theory, (iii) the existence of higher spin conserved charges implies the existence of an infinite tower of conserved charges of arbitrarily high spin.

(i) in d=4, a unique stress tensor plus one higher-spin current is enough to uniquely fix the theory; (ii) in d=3, one unique stress tensor plus two higher-spin currents is enough to uniquely specify the theory; and (iii) in d=2, one unique stress-tensor plus two higher-spin conserved charges is enough to uniquely determine the theory.
